faqs.a: An interest-bearing deposit account that usually pays more than regular savings while keeping your money liquid. In the US, bank MMAs are FDIC-insured; money market funds (a different product) are not.
faqs.q: What is a money market account?

faqs.a: APY includes the effect of compounding over a year; APR is the simple rate before compounding. For comparing savings accounts, APY is the number that matters.
faqs.q: APY vs APR - what is the difference?

faqs.a: At an insured bank, deposits are protected up to the insurance limit ($250,000 per depositor in the US). The main risk is inflation eroding purchasing power, not losing principal.
faqs.q: Is a money market account safe?

faqs.a: Most MMAs compound daily and credit monthly. This calculator compounds monthly, which is within a few dollars of daily compounding for typical balances.
MMAs keep money liquid with a variable rate; CDs lock a fixed rate for a term with early-withdrawal penalties. For emergency funds, MMA liquidity usually wins.

money-market-account-calculator.formula:
Monthly rate r = APY / 12 / 100; months n = years x 12
Future value = deposit x (1 + r)^n + monthly x (((1 + r)^n - 1) / r)
Interest earned = future value - total contributions
howTo: Enter any monthly contribution (0 if none).
Enter the APY as a percentage.
Read your projected balance, total contributions, and interest earned.
keyFacts: A money market account (MMA) is an interest-bearing deposit account, usually paying more than regular savings.
MMA interest typically compounds daily or monthly - this calculator compounds monthly at APY/12.
APY (annual percentage yield) already includes compounding; APR does not.
In the US, MMAs at banks are FDIC-insured up to $250,000 per depositor.
Rates are variable - banks can change your APY any time, so treat projections as scenarios.
Monthly contributions matter more than rate-chasing: $200/month beats a 1% better APY on a small balance.

money-market-account-calculator.workedExample:
$10,000 deposit, $200/month, 4% APY, 5 years:
1. Monthly rate = 0.3333%, n = 60 months. Growth factor = 1.003333^60 = 1.22102.
2. Deposit grows to 10,000 x 1.22102 = $12,210.23
3. Contributions grow to 200 x (0.22102 / 0.0033333) = $13,261.36
4. Future value = $25,471.59; you contributed $22,000, so interest earned = $3,471.59.
